texts.preamble: Dr.George Joseph vs State Of Kerala on 20 January, 2022 Author: K.Haripal Bench: K.Haripal Crl.M.C.4785/2021 1 In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present The Honourable Mr. Justice K.Haripal Thursday, The 20Th Day Of January 2022 / 30Th Pousha, 1943 Crl.Mc No. 4785 Of 2021 Cmp 4187/2010 In Cc 525/2005 Of Judicial First Class Magistrate Court -Ii, Kochi Petitioner/1St Accused: Dr.George Joseph Proprietor, Jishy Hospital, Mundamveli, Kochi-7 By Adv K.A.Salil Narayanan Respondents/State & Complainant: 1 State Of Kerala Represented By Public Prosecutor, High Court Of Kerala, Ernakulam, Pin-682 031 2 The Drug Inspector, Office Of The Assistant Drugs Controller, Ernakulam, Pin-682 032 By Sri. Gracious Kuriakose, Addl.Director General Of Prosecution By Hrithwik C.S., Senior Public Prosecutor This Criminal Misc. Case Having Come Up For Admission On 20.01.2022, The Court On The Same Day Passed The Following: Crl.M.C.4785/2021 2 O R D E R
texts.facts: The petitioner is the first accused in Annexure A1 complaint preferred by the 2nd respondent alleging offence under Section 3A (sic) of the Kerala Drugs and Other Stores (Unlawful Possession) Act, 1971, hereinafter referred to as the Act. The petitioner is a registered medical practitioner and proprietor of M/s.Jishy Hospital at Mundamveli, Kochi. The prosecution allegation is that on getting reliable information that drugs and other stores belonging to the Health Department of Kerala are unlawfully possessed and dealt with by the 2nd accused M/s. Das Enterprises, Pandikudi, Kochi, on 22/04/2002, the complainant/Drug Inspector and party, conducted an inspection in the premises of the accused and found that they had purchased, possessed and sold other stores belonged to Kerala Health Services. The Drug Inspector seized relevant documents under a mahazar and reported the matter to the Court. On the very same day he inspected the hospital of the petitioner, the 1st accused, in continuation of the earlier inspection in the premises of the 2nd accused, and found that the petitioner had stocked following 'other stores' as defined under Section 2(d) of the Act with marking 'Kerala Govt. supply' : 1. Mediflon IV Cannula with PTTE Radio opaque catheter and injection valve-66 Nos; Ref:- Art/No.4020222 lot No.B0570/285 2. Mediflon IV Cannula with PTTE Radio opaque catheter and injection valve-66 Nos; Ref:- Art/No.4020222 Lt No.B0570/286 From the label of the articles seized it was very clear that the marking 'Kerala Govt. Supply' was purposely hidden by applying a price sticker clandestinely causing disappearance of the above official marking. Thus it was evident that the other stores seized from the vicinity of the petitioner issued by the 2nd accused belonged to Government of Kerala, intended to be used in Government Hospitals under the Health Services Department. At the time of inspection, the accused persons could not give satisfactory explanation for the possession of the above 'other stores' in their possession. Thus the complainant seized the articles and connected documents under a mahazar and produced before Court on 23/04/2002 with the report. According to the complainant, it is clear that the petitioner had unlawfully stocked and dealt with other stores IV Cannula, punishable under Section 3(b) of the Act. The accused had no authority to possess the same without showing satisfactory account as to how the suspected articles came into their possession. Those items were intended to be supplied to Government hospitals freely and obtaining the same without acceptable Dr.George Joseph vs State Of Kerala on 20 January, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118052422/ 2 accounts is an offence against the State. Thus the Drug Inspector strongly opposed the prayer in the Criminal M.C. 2.
texts.arguments: According to the Drug Inspector, if any person found in possession of 'other stores' including such stores, the seal or mark has been removed, defaced or in any manner tampered with, and which is or are reasonably suspected of being stolen or unlawfully obtained, and if he cannot account satisfactorily as to how he came into possession thereof, be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months or which may extend to two years and with fine. According to the Drug Inspector, after obtaining 'other stores' through unlawful means, he cannot be heard to say that he possessed it under a bill. 3. According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the second accused is a licensed chemist and the petitioner, who is running a hospital, had obtained those 'other stores' under proper invoice. Referring to the list of documents, especially cash/credit bills issued by the 2nd respondent in favour of the petitioner, the learned counsel pointed out that the petitioner had procured the items by paying price, he had bona fide obtained the items from an authorised druggist paying the consideration; there is no allegation that he had stolen it from the hospital but was purchasing it from a licensed drug dealer. He had purchased it under valid bills. The prosecution has no case that the bills are fake. The counsel also submitted that the petitioner is terminally ill, undergoing treatment for cancer and related ailments. 4. Even though the learned Additional Director General of Prosecution has submitted that the petitioner does not get the protection as in the case of a proceedings under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act on the strength of the invoice, he has not disputed the submission that the petitioner is terminally ill, undergoing treatment for cancer. 5. The said Act was enacted for the purpose of punishing unlawful possession of drugs and other stores belonging to the Health department of the Government of Kerala. As pointed out by the Drug Inspector in the objection dated 01.12.2021, 112 Mediflon IV cannula with PTTE Radio opaque catheters and injection valves were seized by the 2nd respondent on inspecting the hospital run by the petitioner. Earlier he had inspected the premises of the second accused who is a licensed druggist, on getting reliable information that he is in unlawful possession of drugs and other stores supplied to Government hospitals. 8. In this connection, it is appropriate to extract Section 3(a) and (b) of the Act: "3. Unlawful possession of drugs or other stores. If any person is found or is proved to have been in possession of (a) any drug having any seal or mark on it or on packages or containers thereof indicating that it belongs to the Health Department, the Animal Husbandry Department or the Department of Indigenous Medicine of the Government of Kerala, or having such seal or mark removed, defaced or in any manner tampered with; or (b) other stores including such stores the seal or mark over which has been removed, defaced or in any manner tampered with, and which is or are reasonably suspected of being stolen or unlawfully obtained, such person shall, if he cannot account satisfactorily as to how he came into possession thereof, be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months but which may extend to two years and with fine which shall not be less than one thousand rupees: Provided that the court may for any adequate and special reasons to be mentioned in the judgment, impose a sentence of imprisonment for a term of less than six months or of fine of less than one thousand rupees or of both imprisonment for a term of less than six months and fine of less than one thousand rupees. "
